sources.quote: In Ontario the CVOR system is administered by the Ministry of Transportation and covers operators of trucks registered above 4,500 kg
sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Operator's Registration (CVOR) | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: CVOR is the registration system that tracks the safety performance of truck and bus operations in Ontario. A CVOR certificate is required to operate trucks having a registered plated weight (or actual weight) over 4,500 kilograms (9,920 lbs) and buses designed to carry 10 or more passengers. This rule applies to vehicles that are plated in Ontario, the United States or Mexico and that travel in Ontario.

sources.quote: the customs security obligation now sits with the importer, who registers in the CARM Client Portal, obtains a business number and posts their own security for Release Prior to Payment
sources.title: Customs Notice 25-22: End of Release Prior to Payment (RPP) Transition Period
sources.evidence: As of May 20, 2025, all importers who require release prior to payment of duties must have posted their own financial security in the CARM Client Portal. Importers that have not done so are not eligible for release prior to payment. A 180-day transition period was provided following CARM implementation and extended to May 20, 2025 to allow time for importers to obtain financial security.

sources.quote: from the start of 2026 a broker's business number can generally no longer be used to release commercial goods on an importer's behalf
sources.title: What we heard report: Consultation on the use of the customs broker business number (BN) following importer of record legislative changes
sources.evidence: The temporary measure allowing customs broker BN use was extended until December 31, 2025. As of January 1, 2026, following amendments to the Customs Act, customs brokers become jointly and severally liable with the importer and owner of the goods for any amounts owing in duties and taxes when submitting declarations using their own BN. The CBSA is considering scenario-specific exemptions in which importers can authorize customs brokers to do business with the CBSA on their behalf even though the importer is not yet registered in CARM.

sources.quote: taking the position that classifying company drivers as contractors can contravene the Canada Labour Code
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (Labour Program)
sources.title: Government of Canada undertakes inspection blitz to crack down on driver misclassification in trucking - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Worker misclassification happens when a worker is categorized as an independent contractor when they should be an employee. This is an illegal practice under the Canada Labour Code that strips workers of their rights to minimum wage, paid leaves, and occupational health and safety protections. A large-scale misclassification and occupational health and safety inspection blitz in the road transportation industry was carried out in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area from December 1-5, 2025, conducting over 250 inspections.

sources.quote: generally from 4,500 kg gross vehicle weight rating up, are expected to appear in the provincial register of owners and operators of heavy vehicles
sources.publisher: Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec (SAAQ)
sources.title: Registration in the register of owners and operators of heavy vehicles - SAAQ
sources.evidence: Heavy vehicles are defined as those with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 4,500 kg or more. To be authorized to operate a heavy vehicle, owners and operators are required to register in the Registre des propriétaires et des exploitants de véhicules lourds of the Commission des transports du Québec. This applies to owners and operators of heavy vehicles registered in Québec as well as those registered outside Canada but operated in Québec.

sources.quote: Every province runs an equivalent regime under National Safety Code Standard 14, coordinated through the CCMTA
sources.publisher: Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA)
sources.title: National Safety Code for Motor Carriers Standard 14
sources.evidence: Standard 14 covers the Motor Carrier Safety Rating Process. The National Safety Code (NSC) is a set of 16 standards developed by the member jurisdictions of CCMTA in consultation with the motor carrier industry; a safety rating is an evaluation developed pursuant to NSC Standard 14 (Safety Rating – August 2009).

sources.title: Commercial carrier certificates and operating status | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: A Safety Fitness Certificate (SFC) is required for carriers who own a truck or trailer with a registered weight of 11,794 kg or more operating solely within Alberta, or a truck or trailer with a registered weight of more than 4,500 kg used to transport goods on a highway outside of Alberta. Certificates are issued for a maximum 3-year term with a Federal or Provincial operating status.

sources.quote: Trucking HR Canada's research has for several years described tens of thousands of unfilled seats and an ageing workforce
sources.title: Labour Market Information | Trucking HR Canada
sources.evidence: In Q1 2026, there were 13,310 truck driver job vacancies with a 4.7% job vacancy rate. The average worker in trucking and logistics is older than in other industries, with 27% of workers over the age of 55 compared to 21% in the general labour force; on average, 13,675 workers retire from trucking each year, and labour market information forecasts a need that could exceed 40,000 drivers between now and 2030.
